text:
tara: Quick sync after the postmortem: we need a repeatable comms pattern for recurring inference timeouts. Who will own the public status entry vs the customer brief?

gabe: I can take the status page short form. Proposal: 3 lines - impact, mitigations, next update. Keep it non-specific about timings.

veli: I'll draft the 1-paragraph customer brief template (non-technical) and include a 2-sentence 'what we're changing' section.

rachel: Legal/security want explicit redaction rules and an RCA sharing policy. Their current preference: public summary for all affected customers; detailed RCA only to enterprise customers on request after security redaction.

tara: Timeline suggestion: acknowledge within 2 hours, customer brief within 36 hours, and final RCA availability window noted (e.g., released after redaction, target 7 business days). Agree?

gabe: 2h/36h/7bd works. For status page wording, avoid promising restore times.

veli: Draft status blurb:
```
We are investigating intermittent inference timeouts impacting a subset of API requests.
Impact: Some requests may see elevated latency or timeouts.
Mitigation: Immediate fallback routing and capacity adjustments applied.
Next update: within 2 hours.
Customer brief: published within 36 hours.
RCA sharing: summary available to affected customers; detailed RCA available to enterprise customers after redaction review.
```

rachel: Please add a link in the status history to prior related incidents so customers can see recurrence. Also I'll circulate the redaction checklist: remove internal hostnames, customer-specific IDs, and sensitive config or keys; security sign-off required.

tara: Action items: gabe (status blurb) due in 30m; veli (customer brief template) due in 12h; rachel (redaction checklist + assign security reviewer) due in 24h. Comms-bot: set reminders.

comms-bot: Reminders set: status blurb due 30m, brief template due 12h, security review due 24h.

gabe: I'll post draft to the shared comms doc and ping this thread when live.

veli: I'll include a short 'recurrence note' at the top of the brief so customers know we are tracking patterns and adjusting autoscaling heuristics. Keep it plain-language.

tara: Great. Final note: concise public wording, explicit redaction policy, linkable history for enterprise auditing, and no MTTR promises. We'll reconvene if anything changes.
